issue: The Reuby Issue 4 - Soup of Story

members.name: Katherine Faulkner
members.bio: Katherine is a DPhil in Environmental Research. A palaeontologist by day, she finds whimsy in the Reuben dinosaur motif. A Reuby-ologist by night, she finds joy in the ingredients that the Reuben Community provides to make The Reuby a comforting college soup. She hopes you enjoyed this issue and that you look forward to the many more to come!

members.name: Daniel Revach
members.bio: Daniel is a DPhil student in Experimental Psychology. A member of the first Reuben cohort (a dino indeed), he witnessed The Reuby steadily grow in splendour – its editorial team, the quality of its publications, and its role as the voice of the people of Reuben College. Issue 4 continues to embody this very friendship, craft, and vision – in each page and every word.

members.name: Megan Phillips
members.bio: Megan is an MSt US History student currently researching the influence of nineteenth-century women’s magazines (how appropriate!). While she could have sworn she would never get involved in anything at Reuben, here she is, getting involved. She has greatly enjoyed working on the magazine, but her greatest legacy is changing Reuben’s mascot to a dinosaur. Dinosaurs? At Reuben? Groundbreaking.

members.name: Prenika Anand
members.programme: Reuben Alumnus, PhD Candidate in Safety of Artificial Intelligence: University of York
members.bio: Prenika Anand is a Reuben Alumnus currently pursuing a PhD in Safety of Artificial Intelligence at the University of York. Her research focuses on the psychological risks of human-AI interactions within assisted living for older adults. She graduated with an MSc in Applied Digital Health from the University of Oxford. Prenika has been a member of The Reuby team since 2023, contributing to the Humans of Reuben section since inception.

members.name: Proshanto Chanda
members.bio: Proshanto is a first year DPhil student in Biomedical Engineering, researching ways to use machine learning to automate medical image analysis. Proshanto previously wrote articles for and ran a personal blog online, but when he realised that this wasn’t getting him the romantic attention that he wanted, he decided that criticising and editing other people’s writing was far, far easier instead.

members.name: Jake Neuberger
members.programme: MPhil in Global and Area Studies
members.bio: Jake is pursuing an MPhil in Global and Area Studies, following almost four years of collaborating with artists at risk. His research looks to expound on transnational and non-state interactions concerning creativity, memory, mobility, and thought. He chose to join The Reuby to uplift student stories, and is proud to have supported this issue's layout and graphic design.

members.name: Jayroop Ramesh
members.bio: Jayroop Ramesh is a final year DPhil candidate in Computer Science and actively researches on automating the radiological workforce. To assuage his guilt of betraying humanity for a marginally financially secure life, he writes, and edits for The Reuby Magazine.

members.name: Eliza Rayner
members.bio: Eliza is a final-year DPhil student in evolutionary microbiology and a member of The Reuby team since 2023. Although she intended to focus on writing her thesis this year, the pull of The Reuby proved too strong, and she returned to provide some minor assistance with finishing the magazine's layout and design. As she prepares to leave Reuben, she will take very fond memories of her time working on the Reuby!

members.name: Puyu Wang
members.role: IT Officer and Webmaster (Maintainter of this Website)
members.bio: Puyu is another DPhil student at Reuben College who spends much of their time helping computers understand the nuances of human culture. Puyu also maintains The Reuby website, https://the-reuby.github.io/, where all past issues of The Reuby, including this one, can be accessed. Puyu joined The Reuby because they believe every individual deserves the opportunity to express their views and be treated as an end in themselves. Also because, quite frankly, The Reuby is very cool and full of cool people doing cool things.
